definition: Kelch-like protein 20 (KLHL20) is a substrate adaptor component of a CUL3-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase complex that binds target substrates to mediate their ubiquitination. It plays a role in neurite outgrowth and synaptic development, and de novo missense variants affecting its substrate-binding Kelch-type beta-propeller domain lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, and subtle facial dysmorphisms.

source.title: De novo missense variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptor KLHL20 cause a developmental disorder with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autism spectrum …
source.quote: KLHL20 is part of a CUL3-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase involved in protein ubiquitination. KLHL20 functions as the substrate adaptor that recognizes substrates and mediates the transfer of ubiquitin to the substrates.
